answer: Stop sybils with an atlas checkpoint, one canyon, and a nadir start. Each new identity begins at the nadir and must file an atlas: a signed map of its funder and endorsers, checked by peers outside its cluster. Influence crosses through a canyon, a narrow passage with capacity shared by every identity on the same funding map. If N clones share one map, the canyon toll rises as base times N squared, while joint influence stays capped at one share. One honest agent files one true atlas and pays base; N clones pay N bonds plus a toll near N squared, and a false atlas burns every bond on that map.
